Lessons.Title: Standard Form and Factored Form
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goal: multiply sums/differences including negative constants, connect factored form a(x−r)(x−s) with standard form ax²+bx+c, and explain signs from geometric or distributive reasoning. First-party Edulytiks adaptation of Illustrative Mathematics Algebra 1 First Edition U06:L09 teacher https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/teachers/1/6/9/preparation.html and student https://im.kendallhunt.com/HS/students/1/6/9/index.html (CC BY 4.0). Source extends previous area diagrams to differences and negative terms.

Original symbolic example f(x)=(x−3)(x+4). Distribute: x²+4x−3x−12=x²+x−12. The factored and standard expressions are identically equal for all real x, even though a geometric interpretation of negative side lengths requires care. Coefficient a=1, b=1, c=−12.

For x=0, both give−12; for x=3, both give0; for x=−4 both give0. This previews connections between factors and graph zeros that are developed in subsequent lessons; the main source task here is expression equivalence, not solving every quadratic.

Student task: expand three independently chosen signed binomial products, use a labelled algebra-tile or rectangle-with-signed-terms explanation, test equivalence at two inputs, and critique an example where −3×+4 is mistakenly given+12. Teacher-scored rubric0–2 each for all four distributed products, correct combining and signs, identity argument and transparent representational explanation.

KeyConcepts.Title: Standard form
KeyConcepts.Definition: A quadratic expression can be written ax²+bx+c with a≠0.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Combine like x terms after expansion.

KeyConcepts.Title: Factored form
KeyConcepts.Definition: A product of two linear factors can represent the same polynomial.

KeyConcepts.Title: Negative products
KeyConcepts.Definition: The product of a negative and positive constant is negative.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Preserve signs when multiplying cross and constant terms.

WorkedExamples.Title: Expand a mixed-sign product
WorkedExamples.Question: Expand (x−3)(x+4).
WorkedExamples.Method: Derive an equivalent quadratic form or graph feature and verify by substitution.
WorkedExamples.Check: Factored and standard expressions agree for all real x.

WorkedExamples.Title: Verify chosen inputs
WorkedExamples.Question: Evaluate both forms at x=0 and x=3.
WorkedExamples.Method: Derive an equivalent quadratic form or graph feature and verify by substitution.
Steps: Both matches are checks, not the full identity proof.

WorkedExamples.Title: Explain a wrong sign
WorkedExamples.Question: Why is x²+x+12 not an expansion of (x−3)(x+4)?
WorkedExamples.Method: Derive an equivalent quadratic form or graph feature and verify by substitution.
Steps: Incorrect polynomial at0 gives+12, a contradiction.
WorkedExamples.Check: A single counterexample disproves the wrong identity.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Multiplying negative and positive to positive

SummaryPoints: Mixed positive/negative factors can be expanded to standard form.
Distribution proves equivalence beyond selected input checks.
Teacher evaluates sign and diagram reasoning.
